brief.goal: Rebuild the privacy policy on the kit as a calm, honest page in Lisa Bright's first person, keeping every piece of legal substance the migrated body carries and losing the wrong postal address the legacy schema carried and the duplicated sentences.
brief.scope: Ten sections: a text-led hero, eight prose sections cut from the migrated body's headings, and a three-row FAQ. One image. No reviews, no puppies, no price.
brief.done: The page states the controller, what is collected, why, with whom it is shared, how it is secured, the seven rights, cookies and how to reach us, in about a thousand words, and the facts-preserved gate reports nothing missing that `dropped` does not explain.
out_of_scope: the postal address the migrated schema graph carried for a former city (Known Issue 16)
a cookie consent banner (a build change, not a copy change)

angles.name: plain policy in Lisa's voice
angles.hook: the legal clauses kept exactly, the connecting prose written the way Lisa would say it to someone on the phone

angles.name: boilerplate legal notice
angles.hook: a generic UK GDPR template with the company name substituted in
angles.why_not: it would drop the DEFRA transport case and the Kennel Club naming, which are the only parts of this policy specific to buying a puppy

angles.name: policy in a nutshell
angles.hook: a short bullet summary of promises in the style of one of the scanned competitors
angles.why_not: a summary that replaces the clauses loses the lawful bases and the seven rights, and the page would no longer be a policy

strategy.name: plain policy in Lisa's voice
strategy.why: The migrated body already mixes legal clauses with warm prose; keeping the clauses and rewriting only the prose is the change that raises the page without touching its substance.
strategy.trade_off: It reads longer than the shortest competitor policies, which is the price of keeping the lawful bases and the seven named rights.

tool.evidence: A privacy policy asks the reader to calculate nothing; every question it raises is answered by writing to us.

titles: Privacy Policy | BlueStaffyUK Blue Staffy Breeders
Privacy Policy — Your Data at BlueStaffyUK | UK GDPR
BlueStaffyUK Privacy Policy | How We Use Your Data
descriptions: How BlueStaffyUK collects, uses and protects the details you send when you enquire about a puppy, the cookies we set, and the seven data rights you hold.
Our UK privacy policy in plain words: what the enquiry form collects, why we hold it, who it is shared with, and how to have it corrected or deleted.
How we handle your data under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, from the enquiry form to cookies, sharing, security and your right to erasure.

sections.heading: How we look after your information
sections.intent: The opener says who the data controller is, what this policy covers and that it is written to UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Calm, first person, no legal throat-clearing.
sections.why: The migrated body opens with the data controller statement and the GDPR/Data Protection Act 2018 scope, and that is the first thing a reader of a privacy page needs.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — 'Your Privacy Policy Matters to BlueStaffyUK' and 'Data Controller: BlueStaffyUK is the data controller responsible for your data.'

images.prompt: the migrated page's lead silhouette mark, reused at its original path

sections.heading: What information we collect
sections.intent: The two kinds of data, split as the migrated page splits them: what you give us when you enquire, and what the site records automatically.
sections.why: A reader's first question on a breeder privacy page is what the enquiry form takes; all four scanned competitors lead with the same split.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — 'What Information Do We Collect?'; https://www.luminastaffs.co.uk/privacy-policy leads with the same enquiry-form split

conversational: what data does a breeder collect

tree.heading: What you give us when you enquire
tree.intent: Name, email address, phone number, postal address and anything you choose to tell us about your home and family.

tree.heading: What the website records automatically
tree.intent: IP address, browser type, the pages visited and time spent, collected through cookies.

sections.heading: How we use your information
sections.intent: Each purpose with the lawful basis beside it, kept exactly as the migrated page states them so the legal substance is unchanged.
sections.why: The lawful basis list is the legal core of the page and the one part that may not be paraphrased away.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — 'How We Use Your Information' and its five lawful-basis lines

tree.heading: Answering your enquiry
tree.intent: Performance of a contract / legitimate interest.

tree.heading: Telling you about our dogs and services
tree.intent: Performance of a contract / legitimate interest.

tree.heading: Improving the website
tree.intent: Legitimate interest.

tree.heading: Record keeping and administration
tree.intent: Legitimate interest.

tree.heading: Meeting legal obligations
tree.intent: Legal obligation.

sections.heading: When we share your information
sections.intent: The three limited circumstances the migrated page names, including the DEFRA-approved transport case, and the plain statement that nothing is sold or traded for marketing.
sections.why: Sharing is the fear behind the question; the page already answers it with a closed list and that list is worth keeping as a list.

tree.heading: Service providers who help us run the site
tree.intent: Only where they agree to keep the information confidential.

tree.heading: DEFRA-approved pet transport
tree.intent: When delivery is arranged, the details the transport service needs are passed to it.

tree.heading: When the law requires it
tree.intent: For example in response to a court order.

sections.heading: The third-party services we use
sections.intent: The named organisations and tools: The Kennel Club, DEFRA-approved pet transport, and Google Analytics for site analytics.
sections.why: Naming the third parties is what turns a generic policy into a checkable one, and the migrated page already names three.

sections.heading: How your data is kept safe
sections.intent: The technical and organisational measures the migrated page lists: secure servers, SSL encryption, restricted access, staff training.
sections.why: Security is the promise the rest of the policy rests on, and the measures are concrete enough to state.

sections.heading: Your rights over your data
sections.intent: The seven UK GDPR rights as an H3 list, plus the one-month response commitment and the right to complain to the ICO.
sections.why: This is the longest legal block on the page and the one a reader arrives for; it is also what makes the section dial worth mounting.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — 'Your Rights Regarding Your Data (GDPR & Data Protection Act 2018)' and its seven H3s

conversational: how do I ask a breeder to delete my data

tree.heading: Right to access
tree.intent: You can ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you.

tree.heading: Right to erasure
tree.intent: In certain circumstances you can ask us to delete your data.

tree.heading: Right to data portability
tree.intent: You can ask to receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format.

tree.heading: Right to rectification
tree.intent: You can ask us to correct inaccurate or incomplete data.

tree.heading: Right to restrict processing
tree.intent: You can ask us to limit how we use your data.

tree.heading: Right to object
tree.intent: You can object to processing based on legitimate interests.

tree.heading: Right to withdraw consent
tree.intent: Where we rely on consent, you can withdraw it at any time.

external.library_row: ICO — the UK supervisory authority for data protection

sections.heading: Cookies, and changes to this policy
sections.intent: What the cookies do — essential ones for the site to work, analytics ones to see how it is used — and the note that any change to this policy is posted here with a new date.
sections.why: Cookies and the change note are short and belong together; splitting them would make two sections neither of which earns a dial row.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — 'BlueStaffyUK's Cookies', 'Cookies Policy', 'Changes to This Privacy Policy'

tree.heading: Essential cookies
tree.intent: Needed for the site to work.

tree.heading: Analytics cookies
tree.intent: Used to understand how the site is used.

tree.heading: Changes to this policy
tree.intent: Any change is posted on this page with an updated date.

sections.heading: Asking us about your privacy
sections.intent: How to reach us about anything on this page: the email address, the contact page, and the date the policy was last reviewed.
sections.why: Every right on this page is exercised by writing to someone, so the page ends with the address to write to.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — 'Contact Us About Your Privacy', 'Email: staffies@bluestaffyuk.uk', 'Last Updated: June 20, 2025'

sections.heading: Questions we are asked about privacy
sections.intent: Three rows, each answering a question the migrated body already answers: what the enquiry form collects, what the cookies do, and how to have data deleted.
sections.why: An FAQ closes the page with the three things people actually write in to ask, and each answer is already carried by the body above it.
sections.why_source: src/pages/privacy-policy-uk/index.astro — the collection, cookies and erasure passages
